newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia unlikely to meet jobs target - oppn.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia unlikely to meet jobs target - oppn.

text.p: Australian deputy opposition leader Gareth Evans said on Monday the government was unlikely to meet its 1996/97 budget unemployment forecast.
Evans said that in order to meet its forecast for 8.25 percent unemployment by the end of the second quarter in 1997 an average of 17,000 jobs needed to be created each month.
"Subdued business expectations suggest that this new target is unlikely to be met," Evans said in a statement.
"The recent National Australia Bank survey shows that more businesses expect to reduce employment over the next 12 months than increase employment," he said.
"(Australian Treasurer Peter) Costello should now concede that the government's employment forecast is unlikely to be met and get on with the task of repairing the damage."
Costello said earlier on Monday he stood by the government's 1996/97 budget forecast for unemployment.
The government has also forecast employment growth of 1.5 percent in the year.
Australia's unemployment rate was 8.7 percent, seasonally adjusted, in September.
